question: A man walks to a viewpoint and returns to the starting point by his car maintaining a constant speed and thus, takes a total time of 4 hours 45 minutes. He would have gained 2 hours by driving both ways. How long would it have taken for him to walk both ways with the same walking speed?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Replacing the walking journey with a drive (driving both ways) saves 2 hours.

Conversely, replacing the driving journey with a walk (walking both ways) will add 2 hours to the total time.

Given time to walk one way and drive back = 4 hours 45 minutes.

Time to walk both ways = 4 hours 45 minutes + 2 hours = 6 hours 45 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hours 45 minutes.**
